title: Fats Waller at the Capitol
summary: Scott works three or four weeks with Waller and dislikes the room.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: And I had a pocketful of money and I had put a little money in the bank, and the family was living comfortably and I was happy. All right, here come a call from Chick Webb, opening up at the Savoy. No, no, I'm ahead of myself. Fats Waller, Fats Waller, in between, called me. Come to the Capital. Well, I had been visiting there, because when the place opened,

and you get from work and you see the musicians in the band and you hear them, and nobody bothered you then. You wasn't held up or nothing in the streets. Everybody could walk along the streets any time of night, just carefree.

And I'd been there and all like that, and I was acquainted with Fats, and he wanted me to come in on the band for awhile. I did, I did about three or four weeks down there with him, but I didn't like the downstairs. I was more used to Broadway, I didn't like working up there. This was different from Connie's Inn, Connie's Inn was sedate and all like that, and the Capital was a little more honkytonk and stuff.
I didn't care for it, so I got away from it. But I liked Fats, he was great. You know, that guy, they had to put a new piano in there about every two or three months, he was so heavy-handed.
Yeah. But he could play, though, and entertain. Fats Waller was great, he was great, he was great.
What year was this, when you were called by Fats?
Oh, this was between -- right after I came out with Alley and -- '29 and '30, yeah. '29 and '30, yeah. That was before the Savoy opened up.
